summary: TransactionEngine is the observed single commerce authority with a per-actor ledger in flags.foundryvtt-swse.transactions; LedgerService is a pure internal primitive (reads balance, validates, builds credit-delta plans) and is NOT a parallel ledger. Store checkout is routed StoreEngine.purchase -> TE.executeMutationTransaction with lock, verified recovery and post-write verification. Remaining conformance gaps: TE rollback of store purchases does not remove CREATE-bucket droid/vehicle world actors yet reports rolledBack:true (F-STO-001); credit charges outside TE in lightsaber construction, Force Alchemy, progression grants and manual sheet edits (F-STO-002..005); minor UI direct flag writes and a dead legacy TE.execute path.

Ledger record written in the same mutation plan as the charge. purchaseHistory is inert legacy data (scripts/apps/gm-datapad.js:799).

findings.title: Store purchase rollback leaves CREATE-bucket droid/vehicle actors and reports rolledBack:true
findings.observed: executeMutationTransaction applies the merged plan non-transactionally (no transactional:true). ActorEngine applies CREATE (world actors) first; created-actor cleanup only runs when _txnSnapshot exists (transactional mode). On a later failure TE restores only the purchaser snapshot and returns rolledBack:true, so a purchased droid/vehicle world actor can remain without payment. Not covered by any test that injects a failure after CREATE.
findings.intendedOwnership: TransactionEngine guarantees the whole trade fails (OSI atomic trades).
findings.proposedSolution: In TE, track created actor ids (reuse ActorEngine tempIdMap via transactional:true, or a create-ids callback) and delete+verify them in the catch; report indeterminate unless cleanup is verified.
findings.alternatives: Create the asset actors only after the credit/ledger plan has committed (two-phase with compensating delete).
findings.regressionTests: Failure-injection test: store purchase with droid plan, fail ADD bucket; assert no orphan actor and outcome not rolledBack unless verified.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live checkout of a droid with forced failure.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One rollback implementation (ActorEngine transactional) instead of TE snapshot + separate cleanup.
findings.risk: Whole-actor restore semantics (TX-07b) if transactional:true is reused.

findings.title: LedgerService credit-delta plans applied outside TransactionEngine
findings.observed: LIVE: lightsaber construction (workbench -> attemptConstruction) charges credits + creates the saber via ActorEngine.applyMutationPlan({transactional:true}) — atomic-ish via whole-actor restore but no TE lock, ledger record or post-charge verification. DORMANT: InstallRemoveEngine/StructuralChangeEngine apply methods have no live caller (only tests/weapon-phase-5d-i-d-b3-upgrades.test.mjs); ModificationIntentBuilder is orphan and its funds check `if (!hasCredits)` at :226 tests an always-truthy object; UpgradeService world-item branch :707 is documented unreachable.
findings.intendedOwnership: All paid customization through TE (A-10, C-STO-1).
findings.proposedSolution: Route lightsaber construction through TE.executeMutationTransaction(context owned-customization, verify=saber present). Delete or reroute the dormant writers when CUS cleanup happens (see F-CUS findings).
findings.regressionTests: Static guard: buildCreditDelta only imported by TE (ti4a-authority-inventory ratchet); lightsaber construction ledger record test.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Build a lightsaber live; check ledger entry.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One charge path for all customization.

findings.title: Force Alchemy charges credits through ActorEngine with its own compensation
findings.observed: Credits (and Dark Side Score) are written with ActorEngine.updateActor, with partial-application detection and inverse-delta compensation implemented locally; no TE ledger record. Atomicity is handled (tests class-force-v2-alchemy-atomicity) but this is a second credit-compensation implementation.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decision whether crafting costs are TE scope; if yes, add an allowed TE context and charge through executeCreditAdjustment/executeMutationTransaction, keeping DSP/FP handling in Force.
findings.alternatives: Document as approved exception with code comment.

findings.title: Progression credit grants outside TE; GRANT_CREDITS writes credits before its idempotency record
findings.observed: progression-event-processor: credits written (:374/:409) then flags.swse.progressionHistory written in a separate update (:383); if the second write fails the next run grants again. equipment-engine.setCredits (absolute) runs from legacy finalize-integration then grants equipment in separate writes. summary-step stages starting credits + chargenStore flag on the actor before finalization (also an A-15 draft-state concern). None leave a TE ledger record. progression-economy-plan-builder/progression-finalizer credit sets are inside the single finalizer plan (legitimate).
findings.intendedOwnership: Grants: progression-owned; whether they must be TE-ledgered is unresolved (closure report §2).
findings.proposedSolution: Minimum: write credits and progressionHistory in one ActorEngine.updateActor call (idempotency). Then owner decides whether grants go through TE.executeCreditAdjustment with a progression context.
findings.alternatives: Keep grants outside TE but documented as an exception.
findings.regressionTests: Inject failure on history write; assert no double grant on retry.

findings.title: Sheet credit add/subtract and raw system.credits form fields bypass the TE ledger
findings.observed: Any owner can adjust credits from the sheet (ActorEngine.updateActor with a statusFeed entry, not a TE ledger record) or by editing the system.credits input (7 templates). TE has a gm-credit-adjustment context that is unused here.
findings.intendedOwnership: TE single credit authority, unless the owner approves manual editing as an exception.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decision: (a) route the add-credits button through TE.executeCreditAdjustment (ledger + lock), (b) keep direct field editing as a documented GM/owner override.
findings.alternatives: Make the credits field read-only for players.
findings.regressionTests: Ledger record present after sheet adjustment.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Sheet credit edit as player and GM.

findings.title: Store cart and saved-for-later persisted by direct actor.setFlag from UI (A-08 hit is a false positive)
findings.observed: Presentation writes actor flags directly (not via ActorEngine). :1437 runs in a click handler, not during render. getFlag result is mutated in place before setFlag (:1427-1437) — suspected that Foundry diffing may treat it as unchanged; not verified.
findings.proposedSolution: Use ActorEngine.updateActor (or a StoreEngine.persistCart helper) and clone the flag array before modifying.
findings.alternatives: Move cart to client-side session state (OSI UI-only state).

findings.title: Legacy TransactionEngine.execute cart API and PlacementRouter have no callers (legacy C)
findings.observed: No caller of TransactionEngine.execute in scripts/tests/packs; no global exposure. The path has no lock, no ledger record, no verified recovery; PlacementRouter is only imported by TE for it.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete execute() and _compileCartItem/PlacementRouter after confirming no macro use with the owner (class C).
findings.simplificationBenefit: ~210 lines and one unsafe credit path removed.

findings.title: Store view switches re-render the whole app; Holopad caches live SWSEStore instances
findings.observed: currentView changes call this.render() (full AppV2 render). StoreSurfaceService keeps one app instance per actor as its view-model source (has invalidate()). Hypothesis only.
findings.intendedOwnership: OSI performance: UI-only state without full rerender.
findings.proposedSolution: Instrument render count/time per view switch; if significant, extract a StoreSessionModel (cart, filters, view) used by both window and Holopad, render partials.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Holopad stops instantiating a window class as a model.
